subject: Problem making a boxplot .... odd error

messages.author: 473c4ce8ca8f75f2
messages.subject: Problem making a boxplot .... odd error
parts:
Good morning

I have a data set that has variables year and math_1 (and many others).

When I run


with(math1, boxplot(math_1~year,
main = 'Boxplot of Math 1 pct by year'))

I get what I expect. I'd like to use ggplot for its added facilities; but if I run


p <- ggplot(math1, x = math_1, y = TFC)
p + geom_boxplot

I get

Error in object$class : object of type 'closure' is not subsettable

which I do not understand.

I tried using the $ notation for the variables, but that did not help

Any help appreciated

thanks

Peter

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: Re: Problem making a boxplot .... odd error
parts:
On Oct 7, 10:14 am, Peter Flom <peterflomconsult...@mindspring.com>
wrote:

> p <- ggplot(math1, x = math_1, y = TFC)
> p + geom_boxplot()
>
> yields
>
> error: attempt to apply non-function

I think you mean ggplot(math1, aes(x=math_1, y=TFC)). The aes()
function creates a mapping from the data frame variable to the x or y
dimension of the graph. You get that weird error because it's not a
syntactic (R) error, it's a semantic (ggplot) error. When you say "x =
math_1" outside of an aes() call, you're telling ggplot to use a fixed
value for all x. But there's no scalar called math_1 in the
environment, so you get an error. (Why it wants a function there is
not clear to me, but I haven't dug through that part of the code.)
This makes more sense if you compare something like aes(color=Z),
which maps the factor Z in the data frame to the color of the points/
lines/whatever in the plot, using default colors. Versus just color=Z,
outside the aes() call, which usually doesn't do what you want it to
do, or color="blue" which does what you would expect.

You might also try constructing the ggplot object and then doing
summary(p) to get some basic/incomplete information on what ggplot
thinks it's trying to do...

-Harlan

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: Problem making a boxplot .... odd error
parts:
You need to wrap the x and y mappings within aes()

p <- ggplot(math1, aes(x = math_1, y = TFC))
p + geom_boxplot()
